rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-dīn here means reckoning and recompense for deeds; the cited Arabic poetry witnesses recompense, and Qur'an 82:9–10 and 56:86 use it for reward/accounting.
rows.anchor: والدين في هذا الموضع بتأويل الحساب والمجازاة بالأعمال، كما قال كعب بن جعيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the Day of Recompense the Resurrection, when creatures are judged by deeds, good for good and evil for evil, except whom God pardons; authority remains God's.
rows.anchor: يوم حساب الخلائق هو يوم القيامة، يدينهم بأعمالهم، إن خيرا فخير وإن شرا فشر

rows.speaker: السدي عن أبي مالك وأبي صالح عن ابن عباس ومرة الهمداني عن ابن مسعود وناس من أصحاب النبي
rows.claim: This group of early authorities glosses Master of the Day of Recompense as the Day of Reckoning.
rows.anchor: صلى الله عليه وسلم: " {مالك يوم الدين} : هو يوم الحساب

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says it is the day God recompenses servants for their deeds.
rows.anchor: قال: يوم يدين الله العباد بأعمالهم

rows.speaker: ابن جريج
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says it is the day people are requited through reckoning.
rows.anchor: قال: يوم يدان الناس بالحساب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worship clause means humbling, submitting, and lowering ourselves to God in acknowledgment of His lordship, exclusively; al-Ṭabarī prefers this sense to fear and hope because servitude is rooted in abasement.
rows.anchor: وإنما اخترنا البيان عن تأويله بأنه بمعنى نخشع ونذل ونستكين، دون البيان عنه بأنه بمعنى نرجو ونخاف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports Gabriel's gloss to Muhammad: worship means affirming God's oneness, fearing and hoping in Him alone.
rows.anchor: إياك نوحد ونخاف ونرجو يا ربنا لا غيرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic calls a road trodden and subdued by feet maʿbad, and a camel subdued for errands maʿbad; the servant's name reflects subjection to its master, supporting worship as abasement.
rows.anchor: الطريق المذلل الذي قد وطئته الأقدام وذللته السابلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The supplication seeks God's help alone for worship, obedience, and every affair; unlike idolaters who seek aid from their idols, believers serve God sincerely.
rows.anchor: وإياك ربنا نستعين على عبادتنا إياك وطاعتنا لك وفي أمورنا كلها، لا أحد سواك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the request as seeking God's help in obeying Him and in all affairs.
rows.anchor: قال: إياك نستعين على طاعتك وعلى أمورنا كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Help is requested for the remaining lifetime and future obedience, not completed past deeds; enabling the limbs and granting success are divine favor and لطف, whose unequal bestowal is neither mismanagement nor injustice.
rows.anchor: أن يعينه فيما بقي من عمره على ما كلفه من طاعته، دون ما قد تقضى ومضى من أعماله الصالحة فيما خلا من عمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer for help refutes Qadariyyah proponents of tafwīḍ, who claim God must grant each commanded person the assistance needed to act or refrain; otherwise asking help would amount to asking God not to commit injustice.
rows.anchor: أدل الدليل على فساد قول القائلين بالتفويض من أهل القدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worship may precede the request for help because worship and its enabling aid necessarily accompany one another, like saying either that someone fulfilled a need and thereby helped, or helped and thereby fulfilled it.
rows.anchor: كان سواء تقديم ما قدم منهما على صاحبه، كما سواء قولك للرجل إذا قضى حاجتك فأحسن إليك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects the suggestion that the sequence uses a fronted phrase whose intended meaning comes later, a proposal attributed to some inattentive readers and illustrated by Imruʾ al-Qays.
rows.anchor: وقد ظن بعض أهل الغفلة أن ذلك من المقدم الذي معناه التأخير، كما قال امرؤ القيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Imruʾ al-Qays analogy fails: having enough money does not entail giving up desire for more, whereas worship and the aid enabling it necessarily coexist, so their order is not semantic reversal.
rows.anchor: ومن مشابهة بيت امرئ القيس بمعزل؛ من أجل أنه قد يكفيه القليل من المال ويطلب الكثير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated second-person object is idiomatic and more eloquent: Arabic repeats a pronoun with each verb, whether attached after the verb or fronted within iyyāka, though omission is possible when attached.
rows.anchor: كان كذلك إذا قدمت كناية اسم المخاطب قبل الفعل موصولة بإيا، كان الأفصح إعادتها مع كل فعل

rows.speaker: بعض من لم يمعن النظر
rows.claim: Some inattentive readers compare the repeated iyyāka before nastaʿīn to paired repetitions in poetic expressions such as between one person and another.
rows.anchor: وقد ظن بعض من لم يمعن النظر أن إعادة إياك مع نستعين بعد تقدمها في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The analogy to paired phrases with bayna is mistaken: bayna requires two complements, so omitting one makes the sentence defective, while iyyāka nعبد is already a complete clause.
rows.anchor: ليس ذلك حكم بين لأنها لا تكون إذا اقتضت اثنين إلا تكريرا إذا أعيدت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each clause independently needs its object pronoun, just as every verb may repeat its attached object; therefore iyyāka properly recurs before nastaʿīn.
rows.anchor: فكان معلوما بذلك أن حاجة كل كلمة كانت نظيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here ask God to grant steadfastness on the straight path: future success in obedience, right judgment, and avoiding what He forbids, like the request for help in the remaining lifetime.
rows.anchor: في هذا الموضع عندنا: وفقنا للثبات عليه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Gabriel's explanation to Muhammad, the request means that God inspire them with the guiding way; al-Ṭabarī equates this inspiration with granting success.
rows.anchor: قل يا محمد {اهدنا الصراط المستقيم} [الفاتحة: 6] ، يقول: ألهمنا الطريق الهادي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The complete prayer asks to worship God alone, receive help to worship, and be granted the way and method given to God's favored prophets and obedient servants; Arabic poetic usage also makes guidance mean success in a request.
rows.anchor: اللهم إياك نعبد وحدك لا شريك لك، مخلصين لك العبادة دون ما سواك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When God says He does not guide wrongdoers, He means He does not grant them success or open their hearts to truth and faith, not that He withholds clarification of duties, which He gave all accountable people.
rows.anchor: أنه لا يوفقهم، ولا يشرح للحق والإيمان صدورهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The interpretation increase our guidance cannot mean more explanation: God never imposes a duty before explaining it and establishing proof, so this would make the prayer ask for already-provided explanation or for new duties.
rows.anchor: لأن الله جل ثناؤه لا يكلف عبدا فرضا من فرائضه إلا بعد تبيينه له وإقامة الحجة عليه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If increase our guidance means more aid and success, it concerns future deeds, since no help is needed for a completed act; that is precisely his interpretation, and it refutes the Qadari claim that the commanded already have all needed aid.
rows.anchor: أن معنى مسألة تلك الزيادة إنما هو مسألته الزيادة لما يحدث من عمله

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: Some interpret the request as lead us along the path to Paradise in the afterlife, meaning take us there and make us arrive; they compare it with being guided to the path of Hell and with leading a woman to her husband or a gift to its recipient.
rows.anchor: أسلكنا طريق الجنة في المعاد، أي قدمنا له وامض بنا إليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic uses hadā with a direct object, with li-, or with ilā- for directing someone to a path; Qur'anic and poetic usage confirms these equivalent constructions, including omission of a preposition in analogous verbs.
rows.anchor: والعرب تقول: هديت فلانا الطريق، وهديته للطريق، وهديته إلى الطريق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He rejects interpreting the straight path as a way to Paradise in the afterlife: the Prophet's request for aid in worship and the consensus of Companions and Successors show this is a request to remain guided during life.
rows.anchor: وذلك أن جميع المفسرين من الصحابة والتابعين مجمعون على أن معنى الصراط في هذا الموضع غير المعنى الذي تأوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exegetes unanimously define the straight path as a clear, unbending way, as Arabic poetry by Jarīr, Abū Dhuʾayb, and a rajaz poet illustrates; Arabs extend the term to any speech or deed described as straight or crooked.
rows.anchor: أجمعت الأمة من أهل التأويل جميعا على أن الصراط المستقيم هو الطريق الواضح الذي لا اعوجاج فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request means grant steadfastness in the words and deeds God approved and granted to the favored; this is Islam, belief in messengers, holding to Scripture, obeying commands, avoiding prohibitions, following Muhammad and the rightly guided caliphs, and every righteous servant's way.
rows.anchor: وفقنا للثبات على ما ارتضيته ووفقت له من أنعمت عليه من عبادك، من قول وعمل

rows.speaker: علي عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: Ali reports from the Prophet that the Qur'an is the straight path.
rows.anchor: قال وذكر القرآن فقال: «هو الصراط المستقيم»

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali says the straight path is God's Book.
rows.anchor: قال: «الصراط المستقيم كتاب الله تعالى»

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd also identifies the straight path as God's Book.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الله: «الصراط المستقيم كتاب الله»

rows.speaker: جابر بن عبد الله
rows.claim: Jābir identifies the straight path with Islam and says it is broader than the distance between heaven and earth.
rows.anchor: قال: الإسلام، قال: هو أوسع مما بين السماء والأرض

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, in Gabriel's gloss, calls it God's religion, the guiding way without crookedness.
rows.anchor: يقول ألهمنا الطريق الهادي وهو دين الله الذي لا عوج له

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas gives the concise gloss Islam.
rows.anchor: قال: ذلك الإسلام

rows.speaker: ابن الحنفية
rows.claim: Ibn al-Ḥanafiyya calls it God's religion, the only religion accepted from His servants.
rows.anchor: قال: هو دين الله الذي لا يقبل من العباد غيره

rows.speaker: السدي عن أبي مالك وأبي صالح عن ابن عباس ومرة الهمداني عن ابن مسعود وأناس من أصحاب النبي
rows.claim: The report assembled by al-Suddī from these authorities identifies the straight path as Islam.
rows.anchor: قال: هو الإسلام

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the straight path simply as the road.
rows.anchor: قال: الطريق

rows.speaker: أبو العالية
rows.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya identifies the path as God's Messenger and his two successors, Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: هو رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وصاحباه من بعده: أبو بكر وعمر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan affirms Abū al-ʿĀliya spoke truly and advised sincerely.
rows.anchor: فذكرت ذلك للحسن، فقال: «صدق أبو العالية ونصح»

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد بن أسلم
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd identifies the straight path as Islam.
rows.anchor: قال: الإسلام

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن نواس بن سمعان
rows.claim: The Prophet gives the parable of a straight path and identifies the path as Islam.
rows.anchor: ضرب الله مثلا صراطا مستقيما، والصراط: الإسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God calls it straight because it is correct and contains no error; he rejects the claim that it is named for leading its people straight to Paradise, contrary to all exegetes.
rows.anchor: وإنما وصفه الله بالاستقامة، لأنه صواب لا خطأ فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase those You favored explains which straight path is meant: the way of angels, prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous who obey and worship God, as in the promise of Qur'an 4:67–69.
rows.anchor: إبانة عن الصراط المستقيم، أي الصراط هو إذ كان كل طريق من طرق الحق صراطا مستقيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The requested guidance is to the path God described; whoever follows it obediently will be brought to the company and dwelling of those favored, and God never breaks His promise.
rows.anchor: ووعد من سلكه فاستقام فيه طائعا لله ولرسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم، أن يورده مواردهم، والله لا يخلف الميعاد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says those favored include obedient worshippers among angels, prophets, the truthful, martyrs, and righteous.
rows.anchor: يقول: طريق من أنعمت عليهم بطاعتك وعبادتك من الملائكة والنبيين

rows.speaker: ربيع
rows.claim: Rabīʿ interprets those favored as the prophets.
rows.anchor: قال: النبيون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas interprets those favored as believers.
rows.anchor: قال: المؤمنين

rows.speaker: وكيع
rows.claim: Wakīʿ gives the gloss Muslims.
rows.anchor: قال وكيع: " {أنعمت عليهم} [الفاتحة: 7] المسلمين

rows.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
rows.claim: ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd says those favored are Muhammad and those with him.
rows.anchor: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ومن معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse clearly shows that obedience is attained only through God's favor and enabling, since the verse attributes their guidance, obedience, and worship to His blessing.
rows.anchor: وفي هذه الآية دليل واضح على أن طاعة الله جل ثناؤه لا ينالها المطيعون إلا بإنعام الله بها عليهم وتوفيقه إياهم لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording omits the explicit object of bestowed favor because the preceding request and the adjacent phrase identifying the straight path make that favor—the upright path—clear; Arabic likewise omits words recoverable from context, as in lines by al-Nābigha and al-Farazdaq.
rows.anchor: قد قدمنا البيان فيما مضى من كتابنا هذا عن اجتزاء العرب في منطقها ببعض من بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line omits the pronoun hum, recoverable from the preceding word; similarly, the nearby wording those You favored suffices without restating the understood favor or path.
rows.anchor: يريد: متقلديها هم، فحذف هم إذ كان الظاهر من قوله: أرباقهم دالا عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first genitive parse makes ghayr an adjective for alladhīna: the relative phrase is not a fully specified proper name but indefinite-like, so it can take this adjective.
rows.anchor: والذين معرفة وغير نكرة؛ لأن الذين بصلتها ليست بالمعرفة المؤقتة كالأسماء التي هي أمارات بين الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second genitive analysis treats alladhīna as a fully specified definite phrase and supplies a repeated ṣirāṭ: the path of those favored, the path of those outside the objects of wrath.
rows.anchor: وإذا وجه إلى ذلك، كانت غير مخفوضة بنية تكرير الصراط الذي خفض الذين عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two genitive parses have nearly the same implication: those truly favored with guidance to the true religion are not under God's anger and are not astray.
rows.anchor: وإن اختلفا باختلاف معربيهما، فإنهما يتقارب معناهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if ghayr repeats ṣirāṭ rather than qualifying those favored, their evident description as guided by God already implies they are neither objects of His anger nor astray.
rows.anchor: لأن الصفة الظاهرة التي وصفوا بها قد أنبأت عنهم أنهم كذلك وإن لم يصرح وصفهم به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An accusative reading of ghayr is grammatically possible but al-Ṭabarī dislikes it because it departs from the established, widely transmitted reading; it would qualify the object pronoun in عليهم and mean not objects of anger or misguidance.
rows.anchor: وإن كنت للقراءة بها كارها لشذوذها عن قراءة القراء

rows.speaker: بعض نحويي البصريين
rows.claim: One Basran grammarian takes accusative ghayr as an exception from those favored: exclude those not favored or guided, and do not make us among them.
rows.anchor: وقد كان بعض نحويي البصريين يزعم أن قراءة من نصب غير

rows.speaker: بعض نحويي البصريين
rows.claim: The Basran exception analysis appeals to al-Nābigha's poem, where the awārī are excepted although they are plainly not part of the preceding group of people.
rows.anchor: والأواري معلوم أنها ليست من عداد أحد في شيء

rows.speaker: نحويو الكوفيين
rows.claim: Kufan grammarians reject exception: coordinating the negative wa-lā al-ḍāllīn with an exception is unattested, since Arabic coordinates exception with exception and negation with negation.
rows.anchor: وأما نحويو الكوفيين فأنكروا هذا التأويل واستخطئوه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the universally transmitted genitive reading, taking ghayr as an adjective of those favored or as repeated ṣirāṭ; either parse is sound, and he explains the grammatical alternatives because they produce different interpretations.
rows.anchor: والصواب من القول في تأويله وقراءته عندنا القول الأول،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those under anger are the people God describes as cursed and punished in Qur'an 5:60; He informs believers of their fate and shows them the route to salvation out of mercy.
rows.anchor: هم الذين وصفهم الله جل ثناؤه في تنزيله فقال:

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies those under wrath as the Jews in reports transmitted from ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " المغضوب عليهم: اليهود

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عبد الله بن شقيق
rows.claim: Reports from the Prophet at the siege of Wādī al-Qurā identify the besieged people under wrath as Jews.
rows.anchor: أن رجلا أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو محاصر وادي القرى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses those under wrath as Jews whom God has been angry with.
rows.anchor: يعني اليهود الذين غضب الله عليهم

rows.speaker: السدي عن أبي مالك وأبي صالح عن ابن عباس ومرة الهمداني عن ابن مسعود وناس من أصحاب النبي
rows.claim: The report attributed through al-Suddī to these early authorities identifies those under wrath as Jews.
rows.anchor: وعن ناس من أصحاب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم: " {غير المغضوب عليهم} [الفاتحة: 7] هم اليهود

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies those under wrath as Jews.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: " {غير المغضوب عليهم} [الفاتحة: 7] قال: هم اليهود

rows.speaker: ربيع
rows.claim: Rabīʿ says those under wrath are the Jews.
rows.anchor: عن ربيع: " {غير المغضوب عليهم} [الفاتحة: 7] قال: اليهود

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas likewise identifies them as Jews.
rows.anchor: عن ابن جريج، قال: قال ابن عباس: " {غير المغضوب عليهم} [الفاتحة: 7] قال: اليهود

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says those under wrath are the Jews; he also transmits the same identification from his father.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: " {غير المغضوب عليهم} [الفاتحة: 7] اليهود

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: One theological account says God's anger is the imposition of punishment in this life or the next, citing the drowning of Pharaoh's people and the punishment described in Qur'an 5:60.
rows.anchor: فقال بعضهم: غضب الله على من غضب عليه

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A second account understands divine anger as blame for their conduct and verbal reproach or insult.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: غضب الله على من غضب عليه من عباده ذم منه لهم ولأفعالهم،

rows.speaker: بعضهم
rows.claim: A third account treats anger as a real divine attribute, intelligible by affirmation but unlike human anger, which involves agitation, pain, or harm; it is an attribute like knowledge and power without creaturely limitations.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم: الغضب منه معنى مفهوم، كالذي يعرف من معاني الغضب

rows.speaker: بعض أهل البصرة
rows.claim: Some Basrans say lā before those astray is an expendable filler, appealing to poetry and to Qur'an 7:12, which they read as meaning What kept you from prostrating.
rows.anchor: كان بعض أهل البصرة يزعم أن لا مع الضالين أدخلت تتميما للكلام والمعنى إلغاؤها

rows.speaker: بعض أهل البصرة
rows.claim: The same Basran analysis takes ghayr as meaning other than, so the favored are those other than the objects of wrath and the astray.
rows.anchor: أنه كان يتأول غير التي مع المغضوب عليهم أنها بمعنى سوى

rows.speaker: بعض نحويي الكوفة
rows.claim: A Kufan grammarian rejects ghayr meaning other than because lā cannot coordinate with سوى absent a prior negative; he also rejects starting lā with an omitted-negation sense without previous negation.
rows.anchor: لأن سوى ليست من حروف النفي والجحود

rows.speaker: نحوي من الكوفة
rows.claim: The Kufan answer reads al-ʿAjjāj's lā as genuine negation and explains the other poems' apparent filler lā by the negative earlier in each sentence, as in the line about Abū Bakr and ʿUmar.
rows.anchor: إنما جاز أن تكون لا بمعنى الحذف، لأن الجحد قد تقدمها في أول الكلام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers the Kufan analysis: lā cannot begin as an omitted negative or coordinate with other than or an exception; since ghayr can mean exception, negation, or other than, the only valid reading here is negation, making the verse ask to avoid both groups.
rows.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وهذا القول الآخر أولى بالصواب من الأول، إذ كان غير موجود في كلام العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The astray are exemplified by Qur'an 5:77's People of the Book who exceed the truth, follow the desires of already astray people, and stray from the path.
rows.anchor: هم الذين وصفهم الله في تنزيله، فقال:

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: The Prophet identifies those astray as Christians when asked about the verse.
rows.anchor: قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " {ولا الضالين} [الفاتحة: 7] قال: النصارى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عدي بن حاتم
rows.claim: The Prophet tells ʿAdī ibn Ḥātim that those astray are Christians; further routes repeat this identification.
rows.anchor: قال لي رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم: " إن الضالين: النصارى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم عن عبد الله بن شقيق
rows.claim: Reports from a questioner during the siege at Wādī al-Qurā have the Prophet identify the people asked about as Christians, the astray.
rows.anchor: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو محاصر وادي القرى قال: قلت: من هؤلاء؟ قال: " هؤلاء الضالون: النصارى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies those astray as Christians.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد: " {ولا الضالين} [الفاتحة: 7] قال: النصارى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the astray as Christians whom God led astray through their fabrication about Him; the prayer asks for the true monotheistic faith, protection from Jewish wrath and Christian error, and mercy to prevent their punishment.
rows.anchor: قال: وغير طريق النصارى الذين أضلهم الله بفريتهم عليه.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والسدي عن ابن عباس وابن مسعود وناس من أصحاب النبي وربيع وعبد الرحمن بن زيد وأبوه
rows.claim: The cited authorities—through Ibn ʿAbbās, al-Suddī's report, Rabīʿ, and ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Zayd and his father—identify those astray as Christians.
rows.anchor: قال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: " {ولا الضالين} [الفاتحة: 7] النصارى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In Arabic, anyone deviating from the intended road is astray; Christians are so called because they miss the truth and take a religious route other than the straight one.
rows.anchor: وكل حائد عن قصد السبيل وسالك غير المنهج القويم فضال عند العرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both Jews and Christians are astray and under wrath, but God labels each by a true, recognizable characteristic, without listing every blameworthy trait of either group.
rows.anchor: إن كلا الفريقين ضلال مغضوب عليهم، غير أن الله جل ثناؤه وسم كل فريق منهم من صفته لعباده

rows.speaker: بعض أهل الغباء من القدرية
rows.claim: Some Qadariyyah wrongly infer from calling Christians astray and Jews objects of wrath that human acts belong only to people and that God does not cause their misguidance; al-Ṭabarī says this betrays ignorance of Arabic attribution and the many verses naming God as guide and misguider.
rows.anchor: وقد ظن بعض أهل الغباء من القدرية أن في وصف الله جل ثناؤه النصارى بالضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Arabic attributes an act sometimes to its immediate agent and sometimes to its cause: although God creates an act, it is properly attributed to the person who acquires it by power and choice and to God as its creator; Qur'an 10:22 illustrates attribution of sailing to ships though another causes their motion, and 45:23 calls God the guide and misguider.
rows.anchor: ومن شأن العرب إضافة الفعل إلى من وجد منه، وإن كان مسببه غير الذي وجد منه أحيانا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Answering why al-Fātiḥa has seven verses if two contain its meanings: earlier scriptures each included only some meanings, while the Qur'an gathers all of them for Muhammad's community and adds many more.
rows.anchor: إن الله تعالى ذكره جمع لنبينا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم ولأمته بما أنزل إليه من كتابه معاني لم يجمعهن بكتاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Torah is admonition and detailed instruction, Psalms praise and glorification, and Gospel admonition and reminder, but none has a miracle proving its recipient; the Qur'an contains these meanings and more.
rows.anchor: كالتوراة التي هي مواعظ وتفصيل، والزبور الذي هو تحميد وتمجيد، والإنجيل الذي هو مواعظ وتذكير؛ لا معجزة في واحد منها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Among the Qur'an's distinctive merits is its miraculous arrangement and composition: rhetoricians cannot compose even a sura as short as one of its chapters.
rows.anchor: نظمه العجيب، ورصفه الغريب، وتأليفه البديع، الذي عجزت عن نظم مثل أصغر سورة منه الخطباء
